expectations.text: The framing leads with teaching or insight rather than a pitch, matched to a professional feed.
expectations.evidence: The script opens from the customer's lived problem, not from the brand: all four hooks are peer/problem/proof-led ("Fourteen hours a week on reconciliation. Now it's three.", "Every Friday, my team lost half a day just proving the inventory numbers were right.", "How many hours does your team lose reconciling inventory every week?"), with the product name withheld until the 15-30s Solution beat and the CTA held to the end. The choice is explicitly reasoned for the placement: "on a professional feed a checkable number beats a framing device", segment defined as "Ops directors/managers at 3PLs..

expectations.evidence: Partially satisfied. The response opens to the user with a genuine insight rather than an order-taking pitch ('treating founder-to-camera as automatically "fastest" assumes the founder cooperates smoothly... A reluctant subject is usually the slowest part of a shoot'), and the ad itself leads with an outcome stat card rather than the product ('14 hours a week. Down to 3.' at 0:00–0:04, explicitly justified as 'stops the scroll before anyone commits to watching a person').
